intended_object: A function f : ℂ → E "has a primitive" on U ⊆ ℂ (the form f dz is exact on U): there is a function g with complex derivative g'(z) = f(z) at every z ∈ U. This comes from the docstring and the module on complex primitives.
explanation:
The body says exactly that some g : ℂ → E has complex derivative f z at each z ∈ U (`HasDerivAt g (f z) z`). This is the standard notion of a primitive on U. In practice U is open, as in all the lemmas of this file (balls, `univ`, open U). There a derivative at each point of U means the same as a derivative within U, so nothing is lost by using `HasDerivAt` rather than `HasDerivWithinAt`.

The values of the function outside U do not matter. On an open U, any primitive defined only on U can be extended arbitrarily outside U without changing its derivatives on U. So the existential over global functions g : ℂ → E is equivalent to the usual definition, which only asks for a function on U.

On generality: the existential could be written over any nontrivially normed field. But the notion as named and documented ("IsExactOn", "having a primitive" in complex variable theory, i.e. exactness of f dz) belongs to complex analysis. It is used together with Cauchy–Goursat type results that are specific to ℂ. The codomain is already an arbitrary complex normed space. Mathlib has no more general definition of this predicate, and the declaration is itself the Mathlib definition, so it is not too narrow.
